MCP SEP Impact Guide: What Each Proposal Changed and Where It Landed

# MCP SEP Impact Guide: What Each Proposal Changed and Where It Landed

A Specification Enhancement Proposal (SEP) is how a change to the Model Context Protocol is proposed, argued over and recorded. The [official SEP index](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/) is the source-of-truth list of current proposals and statuses. This guide adds what a flat list cannot show: what each SEP changed, which spec revision or extension it landed in, and which protocol methods it touches. To write one, read [how to submit a SEP](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/community/sep-guidelines/). Each SEP is also reachable by number, for example [/seps/1850](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/1850-pr-based-sep-workflow/).

**How to read the Landed column.** This column says how we know where a SEP landed. **cited** : that revision's changelog names the SEP number. **by content** : the changelog or the spec text carries the change but does not name the number. **docs** : only an official docs page (not the spec changelog) names or describes it. **not found** : we found no matching text.

## What the guide adds up to

The official index lists **44 current SEPs** : 43 Final and 1 Accepted. The 43 Final proposals comprise 31 Standards Track, 4 Extensions Track and 8 Process SEPs. Of the 31 Standards Track SEPs, 12 landed in 2026-07-28 (9 cited by number, 3 matched by content), 15 in 2025-11-25, 2 are delivered as authorization extensions and 2 have no spec text. The Accepted proposal is a Process SEP and is listed separately because acceptance does not mean a protocol revision has shipped or the proposal has reached Final.

If you maintain an SDK, a client or a server, start with the 2026-07-28 group. It changes the wire protocol: no `initialize` handshake, new request headers, cache TTLs on list results, multi round-trip requests.

## Final SEPs, by where they landed

Standards Track SEPs change the protocol, Extensions Track SEPs describe an optional extension, and Process SEPs change how the project works.

### Landed in 2026-07-28 (12)

SEP| What it changes| Landed| Methods  
---|---|---|---  
[2577 Deprecate Roots, Sampling, and Logging](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2577-deprecate-roots-sampling-and-logging/)| Deprecates Roots, Sampling and Logging; they stay functional during the deprecation window.| [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/) · cited| `roots/list`, `notifications/roots/list_changed`, `sampling/createMessage`, `logging/setLevel`, `notifications/message`  
[2575 Make MCP Stateless](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2575-stateless-mcp/)| Removes the `initialize` handshake: every request carries version and capabilities in `_meta`. Adds `server/discover` and `subscriptions/listen`; removes `ping` and SSE resumability.| [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/) · cited| `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `server/discover`, `subscriptions/listen`, `resources/subscribe`, `resources/unsubscribe`, `ping`, `logging/setLevel`, `notifications/roots/list_changed`, `notifications/subscriptions/acknowledged`  
[2567 Sessionless MCP via Explicit State Handles](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2567-sessionless-mcp/)| Removes protocol-level sessions and `Mcp-Session-Id`; list endpoints no longer vary per connection, and cross-call state moves into server-minted handles passed as tool arguments.| [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/) · cited| `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`  
[2549 TTL for List Results](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2549-ttl-for-list-results/)| Requires `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` on list and read results so clients can cache them.| [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/) · cited| `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `resources/templates/list`  
[2468 Recommend Issuer (iss) Parameter in MCP Auth Responses](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2468-recommend-issuer-claim-for-auth/)| Authorization servers SHOULD return the `iss` parameter; clients MUST validate a present `iss` before redeeming the code.| [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/) · cited| —  
[2322 Multi Round-Trip Requests](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2322-mrtr/)| Multi Round-Trip Requests: a server returns an `input_required` result and the client retries with `inputResponses`, replacing server-initiated requests. [2133 Extensions](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/seps/2133-extensions/)| The extension framework: optional, composable extensions negotiated through an `extensions` field on client and server capabilities. The field first appears in the 2026-07-28 schema.| [2026-07-28](https://modelcontextprotocol.info/specification/2026-07-28/changelog/) · by content| —

## Method lifecycle across revisions

**✓** means the method is in that revision's core `schema.json`; **—** means it is not. **deprecated** marks a method that is still in the 2026-07-28 schema but deprecated by SEP-2577. **extension** marks a method defined by the Tasks extension instead of the core schema. ## Versions and Verification

Everything is read from one pinned commit of the official repository (`ccaf9102`): 44 current files in `seps/`, the five `schema.json` files, the changelogs of each revision and the official docs pages. The landing tables cover the 43 Final SEPs; SEP-3398 is shown separately as Accepted. The tables were checked by script against the pinned commit; a change upstream needs a re-run.
